Use a factor, character or logical column as a covariate in syntax. Part of the
[Models](models.html) collection, with the other [native engine](model-native.html)
pages. This page needs the development version
(0.11.0).

| | |
|---|---|
| **What it does** | replaces a categorical column on a regression's right side with one 0/1 dummy per non-reference level |
| **Class returned** | `SEMFit` |
| **Syntax** | `y ~ x + group`, `z*group_mid` (label one dummy), `group:m` (one product per dummy) |
| **Limit** | a categorical outcome, mediator or treatment is not supported (see Limits) |

The page cuts `covariate1` into three groups to have a factor to use:

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(medfit)
library(generics)
dat <- transform(mediation_demo,
                 group = cut(covariate1, c(-Inf, -0.5, 0.5, Inf), labels = c("low", "mid", "high")))
base <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + group
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + group
"
```

## Fit and read it

Write `group` where a numeric covariate would go:

```{r}
#| label: fit
fit <- fit_sem(paste0(base, "ab := a * b"), dat)
tidy(fit)[1:7, c("term", "estimate", "std_error")]
```

`group` became `group_mid` and `group_high`, named `<column>_<level>`. The reference
level is the first factor level (`low`), so each dummy is read against it. A character
column is sorted in the C locale, so its reference does not depend on your session. A
logical column gives one dummy, `<column>_TRUE`. The fit equals one with the dummies
written by hand, and `a`, `b` and `ab` mean what they always mean.

## Label or constrain one dummy

A label names one coefficient, so it goes on a dummy, never on the factor
(`b*group` stops with a message that names the dummies). A constraint names a label:

```{r}
#| label: label
pinned <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + group
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + group + z * group_mid
  z == 0
", dat)
tidy(pinned)[grepl("group", tidy(pinned)$term, fixed = TRUE), c("term", "estimate")]
```

`group_mid` in the outcome equation is pinned at 0 and the other rows are free.

## Missing values

Dummies are built from the full column before rows with missing values are dropped,
and a missing value in the factor drops the row once:

```{r}
#| label: missing
dat_na <- dat
dat_na$group[c(3, 40)] <- NA
fit_na <- suppressMessages(fit_sem(paste0(base, "ab := a * b"), dat_na))
c(rows_used = fit_na@n_obs, rows_dropped = fit_na@n_dropped)
```

A level that occurs only in dropped rows gives a dummy with no variation, and the fit
stops with a message that names the dummy.

## Fixed covariates, tests and refits

`fixed_x = "group"` fixes every dummy at its sample moments, and a dummy name fixes
one. `mbco_sem()` refits through a stored factor map, so the data it needs is already in
the fit:

```{r}
#| label: mbco
mbco_sem(fit, paths = c("a", "b"))
```

## Products and the four-way decomposition

`group:mediator1` expands to one product per dummy, each a product term under the
rules in [the native model page](model-native.html). The fit warns that the global
test is not valid with a product, so the chunk silences it and asks for the sandwich:

```{r}
#| label: product
prod <- suppressWarnings(fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + group
  outcome_int ~ b * mediator1 + treatment + group + group:mediator1
", dat, se_type = "sandwich"))
tidy(prod)[grepl(":", tidy(prod)$term, fixed = TRUE) & tidy(prod)$op == "~", c("term", "estimate")]
```

A factor covariate in the mediator equation works with the four-way decomposition,
entering the covariate means through its dummies:

```{r}
#| label: fourway
fw <- suppressWarnings(fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ treatment + group
  outcome_int ~ treatment + mediator1 + treatment:mediator1 + covariate2
", dat, se_type = "sandwich"))
tidy(extract_mediation(fw, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                       decomposition = "four_way"), type = "components")[, 1:3]
```

## Limits

- **A categorical outcome, mediator or treatment** is not supported in the native engine: only a covariate on a
  regression's right side is expanded. The supported routes today:
  - *A two-level treatment or mediator:* recode it as a 0/1 numeric column.
  - *A treatment with more than two levels:* compare two levels at a time. Keep the rows of those two levels
    and code the pair 0/1; each comparison is one ordinary fit. There is no single set of effects for all levels
    yet.
  - *A binary or count outcome or mediator:* use [`fit_mediation(engine = "glm")`](model-glm-families.html) with
    a `binomial` or `poisson` family. Ordinal variables are not supported by any medfit engine.

  These are on the roadmap as separate items, not scheduled.
- **A label, fixed value, start or bound on the factor** stops (`b*group`); put it on one
  dummy. A **constraint** names the label, never the factor or a bare dummy.
- **Ordered factors, a one-level factor, a level that makes an invalid name, and a product
  of two categorical columns** each stop with a message that says why. The full list of
  messages is in the [Troubleshooting guide](guide-troubleshooting.html) and in
  `?"medfit-syntax"`.
- **A refit from raw data** (a nonparametric bootstrap that calls `fit_sem()` on each
  resample) rebuilds the factor each time, so a level missing from a character column's
  resample changes the reference level.
